meta.title: Weekly Fixture: Spreads, Polls and Charts
meta.author: Eve Placeholder

segments: Pretend spreads widen a little. Also, our pretend poll turns gloomy.
Imaginary credit markets had a choppy week as invented central banks kept everyone guessing.
Spreads drift wider
Over the week, the made-up spread index moved from one round number to a slightly larger round number.
Figure 1. Made-up spread index
Source: the fixture author, as at 6 January 2025.
Wider spreads are not automatically bad news. They can simply mean that someone is now being paid properly for a risk that was cheap last month, as a pretend news story put it.
The Pretend Poll
Our invented poll1 asked imaginary staff where three made-up prices would be in a month.
1. Stocks: gloomier

More than half of the pretend respondents expect lower prices, up from roughly a third last time. That swing is large for a poll that usually moves slowly, and it lines up with the drift in spreads described above.
Figure 2. Pretend poll results
Source: the fixture author, as at 6 January 2025.
With contributions from two invented colleagues.
1. The pretend poll had forty pretend respondents.
